answer: Grader-pairwise-agreement graph resists sybils: the system builds a graph of how often each grader pair agrees beyond chance, and an abnormally tight clique of mutually-over-agreeing graders flags a collusion ring. A velvet-smooth cluster whose members echo each other far above the honest baseline stands out as a dense sub-graph; a quill-sketched honest grader agrees with peers only as often as genuine judgment coincides. The over-agreement clique is a structural signature no independent grading produces, and its members' weight is discounted.
